title: buildclamp erratum predicate v1
description: A signed correction: statements matching these criteria overstate a tier, because of this finding. A signed statement is immutable and may be read in 2036; if a release is later found to have overstated a tier, every statement it signed is wrong and there is no way to unsign one. This is how that is corrected. Apache-2.0 and in this tool deliberately: a correction channel only the vendor's own customers could use would not be a correction channel. This file is normative; the $id is an identifier and is never fetched.

id.description: A stable identifier, so a verifier can say which correction applied.

capability.description: The capability whose tier was overstated, or absent for a whole-statement finding.

corrected_tier.description: What the tier should be read as instead.

matches.description: Every field present must match. An erratum with NO criteria matches NOTHING rather than everything — the permissive reading of an empty filter would let one malformed document invalidate every attestation a customer holds. An erratum matching nothing is legal: a correction published before anyone has built with the affected release corrects nothing yet and must still be publishable.
